body:
_Migrated from issue #1301, filed 2026-08-02._

Surfaced while establishing a clean-main baseline for #1300, not by looking for it.

## Symptom

`tests/unit/test_script_import_side_effects.py::TestImportIsSideEffectFree::test_import_creates_no_lockfile` fails intermittently under `pytest -n auto`, and **the failing parameter moves between runs**:

| Run | Failing parameter |
|---|---|
| 1 | `[ingest_processor]` |
| 2 | `[kindle_epub_fixer]` |

It passes reliably when the same tests are run in isolation, and it does **not** appear in every parallel run — the clean-`origin/main` baseline run for #1300 did not include it, while two other full runs did.

## Why it matters

This is the false-red half of FAILURE-MODES class 9. A test that fails on a rotating parameter trains readers to dismiss the file, which is exactly how a genuine red in it would get waved through. It also makes "is this failure pre-existing?" cost two extra full-suite runs every time a PR touches anything — that is what it cost on #1300.

## Likely cause

The test asserts that *importing* a script creates no lockfile. Under `-n auto` several workers import the same modules against the **same on-disk lock path** at overlapping times, so worker A observes the lockfile worker B legitimately created. The parameter that loses the race is whichever import happens to overlap, which explains why it moves.

That is a shared-fixture problem, not a product bug — the lock path needs to be per-worker (`tmp_path` / `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER`), or these cases need to be serialised.

## Not the fix

Quarantining it would silence a real signal about import-time side effects. The lock path should be isolated per worker so the assertion means what it says.

## Repro

```
cd repo && PYTHONPATH=scripts:. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit tests/smoke -q -p no:randomly -n auto --timeout=120
```

Run it two or three times; the parameter rotates.
title: test_script_import_side_effects is racy under xdist: the lockfile assertion fails on a different parameter each run
